Commentary.Commentary: That's a wrap - A thoroughly entertaining Sunday comes to an end. The day began with Bangladesh Women defeating the Dutch. Though to their credit, the Netherlands did challenge their counterparts on their World Cup debut. Followed by that, India crushed Pakistan by 64 runs to grab crucial points and set their sails nicely. Moving forward, there's a day's break and action will resume on 16th June, Tuesday, with another exciting double-header. New Zealand Women take on Sri Lanka Women, followed by England Women going up against Ireland Women. Both games are scheduled to be played in Southampton, and the first ball of the first game will be bowled at 1.30 pm GMT. So do join us early for the build-up as well. Until then, cheers!

Blue outshines Green - A statement win in the end for the Indians, and they have announced themselves as true contenders. Contributions came from every department, though they would reflect on improving their fielding moving forward and also their Powerplay bowling. They travel to Leeds for their next game against the Netherlands. As for Pakistan Women, batting has been a huge weak link, and it continues to be one. They will have to regather themselves for their next assignment against South Africa Women here in Birmingham. Both games will be played on Wednesday, 17th June.

The victorious skipper of India - Harmanpreet Kaur says she is really happy with the win and thanks the Indian fans who turned up to cheer them. Kaur mentions that she is really happy with the way they batted, as the pitch was a good one and after being under pressure, they did well to get through that phase and score big. She credits Richa for her power-striking by saying she is a quality act and can win the game from any situation. Kaur also adds that she is really happy with the way the team performed with the ball and in the field as well. Kaur reckons that every game is important and today's win will help them go ahead against South Africa and Australia.

The captain of Pakistan - Fatima Sana says that she is disappointed with their batting performance and says the batters need to step up. However, she stresses that there is still a long way to go in the tournament, and the side will look to learn from the setback. Reflecting on the bowling effort, she feels they were in a good position for the first 15 overs, but let things slip towards the end by conceding too many runs. She also points out that the over-rate penalty hurt them. Fatima also rues the dropped catches, acknowledging that catches win matches and admitting it was unfortunate that even the senior players put down opportunities. On a positive note, she feels her side won the Powerplay battle with both bat and ball, but says the batting collapse that followed ultimately cost them the game.
... Let's hear it from the two captains ...

Mandhana and Ghosh pushed India to a competitive score - Smriti Mandhana's classy half-century and a late blitz from Richa Ghosh propelled India to 170. The Powerplay belonged to Pakistan, who removed Shafali Verma and Jemimah Rodrigues cheaply to leave India tottering at 18/2. From there, Mandhana and Harmanpreet Kaur turned things around with a 91-run stand for the third wicket. Mandhana led the charge, surviving two reprieves on 27 and 55 before going on to a fluent fifty, though Harmanpreet fell short of converting her start. Kaur's wicket could have triggered a slide, but Ghosh's explosive 34 off 17 took India to an above-par total, with 38 runs flowing in the final two overs alone. For Pakistan, the missed chances will sting most.

Spin proved to be the crucial currency - Pakistan were pushed into a rebuild, with the run rate taking a considerable dip. Muneeba Ali, well settled, looked to anchor one end, but she was starved of the strike for long periods and was eventually run out. The hammer blow followed soon after, as Shafali Verma had Fatima Sana dismissed for a duck to leave Pakistan reeling at 77/5. The spin choke through the middle overs was so effective that everything came crashing down from there, with India making sure no partnership of substance was ever allowed to flourish.

Promising start turned into a procession - The first six overs made for a story of contrasts. Where India had stumbled to 38/2 in their innings, Pakistan raced to a solid 52/1, their highest Powerplay score against India in T20Is and exactly the platform they needed to chase down a stiff total. They lost Gull Feroza early, but a string of loose deliveries from the Indian bowlers let Pakistan cruise along, with Muneeba Ali doing most of the damage. India were critically sloppy in the field too in the early stages of the chase, fluffing a few chances. But on a used pitch, hosting its third game in three days and turning slow, the spin duo of Deepti and Charani made the difference, picking up crucial wickets to reduce Pakistan from 38/0 to 58/3.

PLAYER OF THE MATCH - Without a doubt, Deepti Sharma wins the award for her outstanding bowling effort. She finished with career best figures, reading 5/10 in 4 overs and also scored a run out in the field. Deepti says that she is very grateful and she loves bowling on such a track, and thanks God for helping her time and again. She mentions that the pitch was offering a bit of turn, and she was intentionally looking to bowl slow so that she could extract that spin on offer, and it worked in her favour. Sharma adds that they get support anywhere they go and play, and says this is what keeps them going.

India crush Pakistan in Birmingham - A rather one-sided affair in the end as the Women in Blue hand a deflating defeat to their arch-rivals. Coming into this game, 156 was Pakistan's highest successful T20I run chase, so the task ahead was always going to be a steep one, and they folded under the pressure of the big occasion. This is India's seventh win over Pakistan in the Women's T20 World Cups, and they just keep extending their dominance over their neighbours.

Commentary.Commentary: Richa Ghosh missed a definite chance here to dismiss Aliya Riaz as she chose an underarm throw that missed the stumps, allowing the Pakistani batter to survive a run-out scare.

Oh, what happened there? Drifting down leg on a fractionally fuller length, and Riaz tries to work it across but fails to get her bat in front of the pad. The ball seemingly clips the flap of her front pad before rolling away on the leg side. The batters sense a quick single before Riaz is sent back. Richa swoops across, and there is an appeal for LBW that gets turned down. Richa also senses a run out chance but misses her shy at the striker's end from almost a point-blank range. India go upstairs for the LBW anyway, and while UltraEdge is checked, there is no conclusive evidence of whether the ball struck the pad first or the bat. The on-field call of not out stands as the benefit of doubt is given to the batter.

Commentary.Commentary: DRINKS! Pakistan Women end up at 52 for 1 after the first 6 overs and this also happens to be the highest Powerplay total for Pakistan Women against India Women in all T20Is, informed by Jatin Sapru on air. Muneeba Ali showed the intentions right away by hitting a boundary on the first ball of this run-chase that Pakistan are not going to hang around milking the ball but will go for the chase. Despite losing Gull Feroza, Muneeba Ali, along with Ayesha Zafar, continues to score at a rapid pace. India Women will need to keep making inroads to disrupt the scoring rate.

Lands it on a short of a length, on middle. Ayesha presses back and pulls it wide of short fine leg. Deepti Sharma dives to her left and makes a half-stop. It is mopped by the backward square leg fielder. Two runs taken. 13 runs off the over. Reddy's figures read 2-0-21-0.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 5.6: Arundhati Reddy to Ayesha Zafar, 2 runs.

Commentary.Commentary: From around the wicket, fuller and outside off, this is punched to deep cover for one. The 50 is up for Pakistan.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 5.5: Arundhati Reddy to Muneeba Ali, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Hits the deck hard, tighter line, on top of off. Zafar drops it beside the strip on the leg side and hurries to the other end.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 5.4: Arundhati Reddy to Ayesha Zafar, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR MORE! Width offered and Zafar cashes in! Reddy drags the length back but errs in line, wide on off. Ayesh flashes at the ball and gets it away to the left of backward point for another boundary.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 5.3: Arundhati Reddy to Ayesha Zafar, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! Lovely shot! Fuller in length, on middle. Zafar presses forward and plays a wristy flick. It goes uppishly but clears the leaping mid-wicket fielder for a boundary.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 5.2: Arundhati Reddy to Ayesha Zafar, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: Hits the top of off, Zafar stands tall and taps it to cover.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 5.1: Arundhati Reddy to Ayesha Zafar, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Wide! Sprayed down leg, on a good length. Ayesha Zafar lets it go.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 5.1: Arundhati Reddy to Ayesha Zafar, Wide!

Commentary.Commentary: Just 2 runs and a wicket from Deepti Sharma's over. Arundhati Reddy (1-0-8-0) replaces Shreyanka Patil in the attack.

Fractionally short, on the leg stump line. Zafar goes deep in the crease and gets inside the line of the ball. She shovels it wide of deep backward square leg, where the fielder gets around to her right and tidies up. Ayesha is away with a single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.6: Deepti Sharma to Ayesha Zafar, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Ayesha Zafar walks out at 3 for Pakistan Women.

OUT! TAKEN! Deepti Sharma proves why she is so valuable for India as she strikes in her first over. Comes from around the wicket for the right-hander, this is on a length, on middle. Feroza gets down on a knee and goes for the reverse. She hits it flat and straight to backward point, where Bharti Fulmali takes the catch around her neck. Pakistan Women are 38/1, needing 133 runs in 91 balls.
Commentary.Howout: c Bharti Fulmali b Deepti Sharma
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.5: Deepti Sharma to Gull Feroza, OUT! c Bharti Fulmali b Deepti Sharma.

Commentary.Commentary: Offers flight again, full and on off. Muneeba Ali advances down the track and swings hard. She loses her shape and miscues it off the inner half to deep mid-wicket for one.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.4: Deepti Sharma to Muneeba Ali, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Slower through the air, fuller and on off. Muneeba Ali reaches out in front for the sweep. Gets an inside edge and it rolls to short fine leg.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.3: Deepti Sharma to Muneeba Ali, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Flatter and shorter, outside off. A lot of width on offer. It is there to be put away but Ali cannot beat the fielder at point with the cut.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.2: Deepti Sharma to Muneeba Ali, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Goes past the bat! Dishes out the off-break, full and across the off stump. Ali lunges to smother the spin but is beaten.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.1: Deepti Sharma to Muneeba Ali, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Harmanpreet Kaur has introduced Deepti Sharma into the attack.
Pitched fuller around off, Ali creams it through cover for a single. 12 runs from the over. 26 from the last 2 for Pakistan.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.6: Shreyanka Patil to Muneeba Ali, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: DROPPED! Arundhati Reddy shells one on offer. That should have been taken. An off-break by Patil, full and around off. Muneeba Ali lunges forward and perhaps tries to lift it straight down the ground, but ends up slicing it off the outside half of the bat over backward point. Arundhati Reddy runs to her left but misjudges and puts down a genuine chance. A couple of runs taken.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.5: Shreyanka Patil to Muneeba Ali, 2 runs.

Commentary.Commentary: Into the blockhole, around leg. Ali carves it back to the bowler.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.4: Shreyanka Patil to Muneeba Ali, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! Poor ball and gets the treatment! Drifts one down leg, full in length. Muneeba Ali sits down on a knee and sweeps it hard to the right of the short fine leg fielder for a boundary. Runs are coming thick and fast for Pakistan.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.3: Shreyanka Patil to Muneeba Ali, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: Much fuller on middle, Feroza reaches out in front and sweeps it in front of square, to deep mid-wicket for a single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.2: Shreyanka Patil to Gull Feroza, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! Spot on placement! Dropped short by Patil, on middle and leg. Gull Feroza rocks back quickly and pulls it to the right of deep mid-wicket for another boundary.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.1: Shreyanka Patil to Gull Feroza, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: Change? Nope, Shreyanka Patil to continue.
Play and a miss! On a wider line, outside off, Muneeba Ali tries to cut the length ball through point, but it nips away and beats the outside edge. A very expensive over as 14 runs come from it.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.6: Kranti Gaud to Muneeba Ali, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! This is ordinary bowling from Gaud. Bowls a short ball from around the stump. The ball angles in but sits up nicely for Muneeba, who helps it away with a pull shot, beating short fine leg to her right for a boundary.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.5: Kranti Gaud to Muneeba Ali, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: Hard length, outside off, Gull Feroza square cuts it to deep backward point for a single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.4: Kranti Gaud to Gull Feroza, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! Beats the fielder! Back of a length, from over the stump. Gull Feroza gets enough width outside off and slashes it hard to beat the diving short third fielder to her right for a boundary.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.3: Kranti Gaud to Gull Feroza, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: Short of a good length, on off, Muneeba mistimes the pull shot to the square leg region for a single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.2: Kranti Gaud to Muneeba Ali, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! That's cleverly played! Kranti starts with a full ball, on off. Muneeba Ali sits down on her knee by shuffling across the stumps and nails the scoop shot over short fine leg for a boundary.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.1: Kranti Gaud to Muneeba Ali, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: In-drifter on a fuller length, on the pads. Ali tries to work it away with a flick but misses. She is hit on the front pad and the ball rolls away to the square leg region. Sree Charani moves across and throws it to the bowler, but Feroza is quick to complete the run.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.6: Shreyanka Patil to Muneeba Ali, Leg bye.

Commentary.Commentary: Sliding on with the arm, on a good length. Ali blocks it off.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.5: Shreyanka Patil to Muneeba Ali, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Shorter than the previous ball, on middle and leg. Gull pivots and pulls it to deep backward square leg. They cross.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.4: Shreyanka Patil to Gull Feroza, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Dropped short outside off, Muneeba Ali cuts off the back foot to the off side for a single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.3: Shreyanka Patil to Muneeba Ali, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: DROPPED! A definite chance goes down! Lands it full and around off, and gets it to turn sharply away from the batter. Muneeba is sucked on the front foot to block, but gets a thin outside edge. Richa Ghosh fails to hold on to a catch to her left as the ball pops out of her gloves.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.2: Shreyanka Patil to Muneeba Ali, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: From around the stump, this is slowish on a fuller length, outside off. Lands and turns away to beat Muneeba's attempted sweep shot.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.1: Shreyanka Patil to Muneeba Ali, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: It will be spin from the other end in the form of Shreyanka Patil. Deepti Sharma is at slip.
Pitched in front of the stumps, nips in from a length. Gull Feroza turns it across to mid-wicket. 8 runs off the first over then.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.6: Arundhati Reddy to Gull Feroza, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: WIDE! Slides one down leg, on a good length. Gull Feroza looks to flick but misses. Richa collects it sharply to her left and appeals for caught behind, but nothing doing.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.6: Arundhati Reddy to Gull Feroza, Wide!

Commentary.Commentary: Around off, on a length. Feroza rides the bounce and eases it to mid on.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.5: Arundhati Reddy to Gull Feroza, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Full again, outside off, pushed into the cover region for a single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.4: Arundhati Reddy to Muneeba Ali, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Fuller in length, tailing down leg. Gull Feroza flicks but seems to have got an inside edge back to the keeper. Richa does not grab it cleanly and parries it to the leg side off her gloves for a single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.3: Arundhati Reddy to Gull Feroza, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Around the leg stump, Muneeba flicks it wide of Bharti Fulmali at short fine leg and sets off for a single. Bharti dives to stop the ball, preventing any other run.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.2: Arundhati Reddy to Muneeba Ali, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! Up and over and Pakistan are underway! Width on offer by Reddy, on a length, outside off. Ali slashes hard at it and gets a bit of an outside edge, but the ball flies over and wide of short third for a boundary.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.1: Arundhati Reddy to Muneeba Ali, Four!
